rules.name: Preparation for Honors in the Arts
rules.desc: To qualify for admission, students must identify three courses, at least two of which must be completed by the end of junior year, that have provided the necessary foundation for the honors project. Students are encouraged to consult SAI's Interdisciplinary Courses Guide and Creative Courses Guide to identify courses that provide an introduction to the study of the arts disciplines as well as incorporating the arts in an interdisciplinary context.

rules.name: Thesis Workshop Sequence
rules.desc:
Each Spring, students present their honors projects at a public exhibition and online symposium.
To receive Honors in the Arts, students must fulfill all the requirements and receive an A- or higher on their project and its critical framing.
The Honors in the Arts website provides requirements and further information.

rules.name: Honors Projects
rules.desc:
All accepted projects are eligible for modest financial support for materials needed to complete the project.
Through a yearlong process, students develop a creative thesis project that goes beyond the traditional boundaries of their major.

• Honors projects center research creation, combine two or more kinds of art practice, or blend art and research in some creative yet rigorous way.

• Students can apply with an individual or team-based project. For team-based projects (2-5 students per team), applicants must delineate what expertise each student brings to the project.

• Students must receive at least an 'A-' on the project and its critical framing. Students who receive a grade of less than an 'A-' but greater than 'NP' receive credit for the workshops but do not receive honors.

• Mentorship: Each student works closely with a faculty advisor and a graduate student mentor to develop and complete the thesis project. Students in the program are responsible for setting up regular meetings with their advisors and mentors throughout the academic year.
Requirements and further information can be found here on the Honors in the Arts website.
